Intonation with Lists, Choice Questions, and Non-final Thought Groups

Intonation is the rise and fall of your voice. There are definite and expected intonation patterns in English.  The more you practice listening to and saying the correct intonation patterns, the better you will understand and be understood.

When naming items in a list you use rising intonation for all the items in the list except the last item. You use falling intonation for the last item because falling intonation indicates that the list is finished.

For example:

I follow the three Rs. I recycle ⤴, reduce ⤴, and reuse ⤵.

The rising intonation indicates to the listener that you are not finished and that there are other items in the list.

All choice questions have an 'or' in them and cannot be answered with yes or no. These questions offer a choice between one option or the other.

For example:
Did you recycle that ↗ or just throw it in the trash⤵?

A thought group refers to a coherent unit of speech that forms a whole. You normally separate a long sentence into several thought groups. Non-final thought groups represent all the thought groups that you say before the last thought group of a sentence. The final thought group is the thought group that ends a sentence. You stress non-final thought groups with a normal-rising-normal pattern.

For example:
Paper consumption continues to rise ... a typical office will use approximately 1,000 sheets of paper ... per month ... per person.

Read the following sentences, keeping in mind the different intonation patterns you use:
It takes a large amount of energy  to light, heat and cool a workplace.

images.text: We must look for ways to reduce our environmental footprint and go greener—not just at home, but here at work as well. We need to make small changes at our workplace so we can help protect our environment. If we implement environmentally friendly practices in our office, we can all make a difference.

This year, office equipment will have accounted for a large portion of the energy used in our office — in fact, more than 50% of it. So, if you won't be using your computer screen, turn it off. Computer screens are the biggest users, consuming 10% of the total energy. This happens even when they are on standby. We must reduce our energy consumption. This will save energy, make our office more environmentally friendly, and more cost-friendly.
Our paper consumption is also continuing to rise. We needn't waste so much. How much paper do you think you will have used by the end of a month? The average is about 1,000 sheets per person. We must cut back. We need to significantly decrease our solid waste.

Also, all greenhouse gas emissions need to be reduced. Because electricity generation is a major source of greenhouse gases, reducing the amount of electricity used is the place to start.
Do you leave the water running when you're washing your plate at lunch, or do you turn the tap off? Water is a precious resource. That demand for water is constantly growing. We need to be mindful when using it. We must help conserve our water.
We mustn't allow ourselves to be apathetic! We can make a difference by taking simple steps to be more environmentally friendly. It's the little actions we take that will have added up to big results in the long run. By getting involved, we can all make real impact!
